headline: Highest risk is data leakage: oh-my-openagent handles project code, AGENTS.md, and provider auth data while awesome-production-machine-learning is a non-runnable docs-only list with no isolation or egress, making direct pairwise harm…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a docs-only, non-runnable list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs directly. B can run browsers, subprocesses, and runtime-injected MCPs/hooks, which creates a plausible manual-copy or shared-file bridge, but the pathway is not default and the blast radius is small because A has no execution surface.
conditions: IF B’s browser or MCP output is manually copied into A-related documentation or prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF an operator wires both agents to the same shared file or clipboard, B can carry attacker-controlled text into A’s workflow.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Disable copy/paste of untrusted B output into A workflows.
Use a plain-text sanitizer before moving content between agents.
Review any shared MCP or hook configuration before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent text transfers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B touches project code, AGENTS.md, README.md, session history, and provider auth data, and has broad network egress plus API calls. If the pair shares a workspace or B reads A-linked files, B can leak sensitive local context to third parties by default; A does not materially reduce that risk.
conditions: IF A and B are pointed at the same repository or home directory, B can access files that A does not protect.
IF B is allowed to call external APIs while handling provider auth prompts or session history, those contents can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Separate B from any directory containing secrets or auth prompts.
Turn off B’s external API calls for sensitive sessions.
Use a dedicated OS account for B.
Clear session history before running B on shared machines.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls and secret redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot conflict operationally with B. B can spawn subprocesses, use multiple instances, and write to several config and plugin paths, so overlapping writes are plausible if both are installed in the same user environment. The conflict is not high because A lacks mutable surfaces, but uncertainty about hidden shared paths pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write under the same home-directory plugin or config path, B can overwrite shared state.
IF B runs multiple instances against the same installation, concurrent writes can race on its config files.
mitigations: Place B in a separate user profile.
Lock down writable config directories.
Run only one B instance per installation.
Back up B config files before changes.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A does not produce actionable outputs or facts; it is a static resource list. B can act on code and support workflows, but there is no documented pathway where B treats A’s output as authoritative. Because A lacks runtime behavior, the cascade from A into B is mostly absent, leaving only a weak manual-transfer risk.
conditions: IF an operator manually converts A’s list entries into instructions for B, B may act on them without verification.
IF B is configured to trust pasted content as authoritative, any copied A text can propagate errors.
mitigations: Do not use A output as an execution source.
Require human review before B acts on copied text.
Mark A-derived content as untrusted in prompts.
Use a verification checklist for any A-to-B transfer.
requires-engineering: add source-validation gates before B executes tasks.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source, non-runnable list with no touched data classes, so it does not create a residency or retention issue on its own. B handles provider auth prompts, session history, and telemetry, which can raise compliance concerns, but the pairwise mismatch is limited because A contributes no regulated data. The other agent is cited to show the only meaningful compliance surface is B.
conditions: IF B is used with provider auth prompts or session history containing regulated data, retention and transfer policies must be checked.
IF A is repurposed to store regulated data, its open-source docs-only nature would no longer be sufficient for compliance review.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in B sessions.
Review B retention settings before use.
Disable telemetry where possible.
Keep A free of sensitive content.
requires-engineering: document data-flow and retention controls for B.
